content.title: How Alabamians Can Score Usher & Chris Brown ‘The R&B Tour’ Tickets
content.text: 92.9 WTUG is turning up the R&B heat this weekend with mini concerts featuring Usher Raymon and Chris Brown to celebrate their announcement of ‘The R&B Tour” heading to Alabama.Listen this weekend for mini concerts that highlight the superstar duo, showcasing their legendary music, making way for one of the hottest summer concert events.It’s kind of genius when you think about it, Usher and Chris Brown don’t just headline the tour, their last names are the tour. The “R” and the “B” line up perfectly!Listeners can qualify to win tickets to the iconic show on Tuesday, July 28, at Protective Stadium in Birmingham, Alabama. Click here for more information on the show.“Fans can expect a hit-filled setlist featuring classics and fan favorites, delivered with the showmanship that made both artists global superstars,” said Protective Stadium. “This dynamic pairing brings together generations of R&B, promising an unforgettable night of music, movement, and nonstop crowd energy.”Score Tickets Before They Even Go on Sale: Here’s How to Win with WTUGOpen up the WTUG appTap “Talk to Us Now”Tell us your ultimate favorite song from Usher or Chris Brown to qualify to win ticketsYou must submit your entry by Sunday, April 19, by 11:59 p.m.RANKED: Your Favorite Childhood Bubble GumsFrom long-lasting flavor to epic bubble potential, we're ranking the most iconic childhood chewing gums that defined recess, ruled the playground and stuck with us (sometimes literally).Gallery Credit: Stephen LenzLOOK: Popular children's books published the year you were bornStacker compiled a list of popular children's books published every year between 1920 and 2021 based on librarian and teacher polls, top 100 roundups in media like Time magazine and the BBC, book critic reviews, interviews with children's book authors, and lists of award-winning literature for young readers.Gallery Credit: Joni Sweet1920: The Story of Doctor Dolittle by Hugh Lofting1921: The Story of Mankind by Hendrik Willem Van Loon1922: The Velveteen Rabbit by Margery Williams1923: Emily of New Moon by Lucy Maud Montgomery1924: Tales From Silver Lands by Charles J.
